about.title: Bakersfield Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Most people in Bakersfield don't expect to question the care they receive. You go in for a procedure, a delivery, or a visit to the emergency department, and you trust the people in scrubs. When something goes wrong, the hardest part is often figuring out whether it was an unavoidable complication or a preventable mistake. California law draws that line carefully: a poor result by itself is not malpractice. What matters is whether a provider fell below the accepted standard of care and whether that failure caused real harm. Bakersfield's roughly 373,640 residents share the same local hospitals and clinics, and in 2025 alone 2,245 people were injured in city collisions, many of them treated in emergency rooms working under pressure. We handle medical negligence cases and can review your records, consult a qualified medical expert, and explain the MICRA deadlines that apply to your situation.

whyChoose.title: Why Kern County Patients Choose Us

items.title: MICRA Deadlines Are Short
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from the date you discovered the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself. A 90-day notice must also go to the provider before a suit is filed, so early review matters.

items.title: A Medical Expert Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: These cases nearly always need a qualified physician to explain how the care fell short. Our team knows how to find and work with the right specialist for your situation.

items.title: Know the Cap Before You Decide
items.desc: California limits non-economic damages in malpractice cases, and that cap rises each year. We can explain how the current limit applies to your claim and what is not subject to it.

items.question: My surgery in Bakersfield didn't go well. Is that automatically malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Some complications happen even when everyone does their job correctly, and California law does not treat a bad outcome alone as negligence. A claim depends on showing that a provider departed from the accepted standard of care and that the departure caused your harm. Our team will usually have a medical expert review your chart before giving you an opinion.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Under MICRA, the general rule is one year from when you discovered, or reasonably should have discovered, the injury, with an outer limit of three years from the date the harm occurred. You also must give the provider written notice at least 90 days before filing suit. Because these windows can close quickly, it helps to speak with us as soon as you suspect a problem.

items.question: What does your service cost, and how does it work?
items.answer: There is no cost to you. We handle medical malpractice cases in the Bakersfield area and work on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless there is a recovery in your case.
